questions.question: Who announced the launch of India’s first homegrown semiconductor chip in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajeev Chandrasekhar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rajeev Chandrasekhar**, who is the **Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology** in India, announced the launch of **India’s first homegrown semiconductor chip** in **May 2025**.
 
• The announcement marked a significant milestone for India’s ambition to become a global hub for **semiconductor manufacturing** and reduce dependence on imports.
 
• This initiative is part of the broader **Semicon India Programme**, launched by the government to develop a robust semiconductor ecosystem in the country with a **financial outlay of Rs. 76,000 crore**.
 
• The homegrown semiconductor chip is expected to bolster India's position in the global electronics supply chain, which has been disrupted due to geopolitical tensions and the pandemic.
 
• Semiconductors are the backbone of modern electronics, including **smartphones, laptops, automobiles, and defense equipment**. This development is aligned with the government’s mission of **Aatmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Semicon India Programme:**

 
 
• Launched by the **Government of India** in **December 2021**, the programme aims to establish India as a global hub for semiconductor design, manufacturing, and technology development.
 
• It includes initiatives to attract investments from global semiconductor companies and foster **research and development** in this field.
 
• The programme is expected to create job opportunities and enhance India's capabilities in critical technologies.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Semiconductors:**
 
 
• Semiconductors are essential components in electronic devices such as **microprocessors, sensors, and memory chips**.
 
• They enable the functioning of various sectors, including **telecommunications, healthcare, automotive, and defense**.
 
• India has been heavily dependent on imports for its semiconductor needs, making the development of indigenous chips a strategic move.
 
 
 
• **Rajeev Chandrasekhar’s Role:**
 
 
• Rajeev Chandrasekhar is a prominent Indian politician and entrepreneur with expertise in technology and innovation.
 
• He has been actively involved in shaping India’s digital economy and promoting initiatives like **Digital India** and **Make in India**.
 
• As the Minister of State for Electronics and IT, he has played a crucial role in the formulation and execution of policies aimed at enhancing India’s technological capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Global Semiconductor Market:**
 
 
• The global semiconductor market was valued at approximately **USD 555.9 billion** in 2021 and is expected to grow significantly in the coming years.
 
• The demand for semiconductors has been driven by advancements in **5G technology, artificial intelligence, and IoT (Internet of Things)**.
 
• India’s entry into semiconductor manufacturing is expected to increase its competitiveness in the global market and reduce reliance on imports from countries like **China and Taiwan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Semiconductor Manufacturing:**

 
 
• Setting up a semiconductor fabrication unit is capital-intensive, requiring investments ranging from **USD 3 billion to USD 15 billion**.
 
• The process involves complex technological requirements, including **cleanrooms, equipment, and skilled professionals**.
 
• India faces challenges in terms of infrastructure, supply chain development, and the availability of raw materials like silicon wafers.
 
 
 
• **Global Supply Chain Issues:**
 
 
• The semiconductor industry has faced disruptions due to the **COVID-19 pandemic** and geopolitical tensions, leading to a global chip shortage.
 
• India’s initiative to develop homegrown chips is a step towards reducing dependency on global supply chains and ensuring self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• The success of India’s semiconductor initiative will depend on its ability to attract investments, develop skilled manpower, and create a conducive business environment.
 
• Collaborations with global technology leaders and academic institutions will be crucial for building a robust semiconductor ecosystem.
 
• India’s efforts in this sector are expected to contribute significantly to its **GDP growth** and technological advancements.

questions.question: The "Mission Mitra" was in the news. What does it refer to?

options.text: A new satellite launched by ISRO to study the terrain of Ladakh
A military exercise conducted by the Indian Air Force in freezing temperatures
An underground cave experiment conducted by the European Space Agency
A high-altitude experiment to simulate deep space conditions for Gaganyaan astronauts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A high-altitude experiment to simulate deep space conditions for Gaganyaan astronauts.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Mission Mitra was recently in the news as four astronauts selected for the Gaganyaan Mission began a unique high-altitude experiment in Ladakh.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mission Mitra stands for Mapping of Interoperable Traits & Reliability Assessment.**
 
• Led by ISRO's Human Space Flight Centre and Protoplanet, the initiative aims to simulate the harsh conditions of deep space on Earth.
 
• It utilizes the rugged, high-altitude terrain of Ladakh, which offers freezing temperatures, low oxygen levels, and isolation as an ideal terrestrial analogue.
 
• The mission focuses on evaluating the human machine, testing psychological resilience, stress response, and interpersonal cohesion under extreme conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Gaganyaan Programme__

 __
 
• India's human spaceflight initiative aimed at demonstrating the capability to send humans to low Earth orbit.
 
• It involves designated astronauts like Group Captain Shubhnashu Shukla and P Balakrishnan Nair.
 
 
 
• European Space Agency Caves experiment__
 __
 
• An astronaut training initiative that uses deep underground cave systems to simulate space mission conditions.
 
• Mission Mitra draws inspiration from this program but is conducted in high-altitude terrestrial environments instead of caves.
 
 
 
• ISRO Human Space Flight Centre__
 __
 
• The lead center of the Indian Space Research Organisation responsible for coordinating the Gaganyaan mission.
 
• They collaborate with organizations like Protoplanet and medical experts to ensure astronauts are psychologically and physically prepared.
 
 
 
• Terrestrial Analogue__
 
 
• A place on Earth with assumed past or present environmental conditions similar to those of a celestial body or deep space.
 
• Ladakh serves as this analogue for Mission Mitra due to its extreme climate and isolation constraints.

questions.question: The NVS-02 satellite was launched aboard which of the following launch vehicles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) made public a technical committee report analysing why the NVS-02 satellite, launched on January 29, 2025, could not be placed in its intended orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The NVS-02 satellite was launched aboard a GSLV rocket. **Hence, Option A is correct. **
 
• PSLV is primarily used for launching earth observation and small satellites and was not used for NVS-02. **Hence, Option B is incorrect. **
 
• SSLV is designed for small satellite launches and was not associated with this mission. **Hence, Option C is incorrect. **
 
• LVM-3 (formerly GSLV Mk III) was used later to launch GSAT-7R, not NVS-02.** Hence, Option D is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The failure was attributed to a signal not reaching a key valve in the engine’s oxidiser line.
 
• The issue likely arose due to a loose or failed electrical connector in both primary and backup lines.
 
• Lessons from the failure were reportedly implemented in the November 2, 2025 LVM-3 M5 mission.
 
• GSAT-7R, India’s heaviest communication satellite, was successfully placed in orbit by LVM-3 M5.

questions.question: The term "Yurpeak" was recently in the news. What does it refer to?

options.text: A new vaccine launched for dengue prevention
A digital health monitoring platform introduced by the government
A new insulin pump device developed by an Indian startup
An injectable drug launched by Cipla for obesity and type-2 diabetes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A once-weekly injectable drug launched by Cipla for obesity and type-2 diabetes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Cipla has launched Yurpeak, a tirzepatide-based injectable therapy for managing obesity and type-2 diabetes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yurpeak is a once-weekly injectable medication formulated using tirzepatide.**
 
• **Cipla holds the rights to distribute and promote Yurpeak in India.**
 
• **It is the second tirzepatide brand available in India after Lilly received DCGI approval.**
 
• **The drug targets two major health burdens in India—obesity and type-2 diabetes mellitus.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tirzepatide**__

 __
 
• A dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist used to improve glycemic control and induce weight loss.
 
• Developed by Eli Lilly and approved in India for type-2 diabetes management.
 
 
 
• **DCGI**__
 __
 
• The Drug Controller General of India regulates drug approvals and ensures safety, efficacy and quality standards.
 
 
 
• **Cipla**__
 
 
• A leading Indian pharmaceutical company headquartered in Mumbai.
 
• Known for its portfolio across respiratory, diabetes and cardiovascular therapies.

questions.question: Which NASA satellite, launched in 2012 to study Earth's radiation belts, successfully re-entered the atmosphere on March 11, 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Van Allen Probe A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **NASA’s Van Allen Probe A re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on March 11, 2026, ending a 14-year journey that revolutionized our knowledge of space weather.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mission Objective:** Launched in August 2012, the twin probes (A and B) were designed to study the **Van Allen radiation belts**—zones of energetic charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field.
 
• **Major Discovery:** The mission discovered a **transient third radiation belt** that appears during intense solar activity, challenging the previous two-belt model.
 
• **Accelerated Re-entry:** Originally predicted to re-enter in 2034, the timeline was moved up due to increased **atmospheric drag** caused by the 2024-2026 solar maximum.
 
• **Legacy:** The data helps protect satellites and astronauts by improving predictions of how solar storms affect communications and GPS.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Van Allen Belts__

 __
 
• Named after **James Van Allen**, these consist of an inner belt (mostly protons) and an outer belt (mostly electrons).
 
 
 
• Solar Maximum__
 __
 
• The period of greatest solar activity in the 11-year solar cycle, characterized by more sunspots and solar flares, which expands Earth's atmosphere.
 
 
 
• Van Allen Probe B__
 
 
• The second half of the twin mission is currently still in orbit and is expected to undergo re-entry after 2030.

questions.question: The term “Smog-Eating Photocatalytic Coatings,” is related to:

options.text: A titanium dioxide-based coating that uses light to break down air pollutants like nitrogen dioxide and volatile organic compounds.
A chemical spray used to artificially disperse smog particles in the atmosphere.
A filtration system installed in vehicles to reduce emission of particulate matter.
A geoengineering technique to block sunlight and reduce atmospheric pollution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Delhi government and IIT Madras initiated a study on “smog-eating” photocatalytic coatings to evaluate their effectiveness in reducing NO₂ and VOC pollutants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Smog-eating photocatalytic coatings use titanium dioxide, which acts as a catalyst under sunlight to break down harmful pollutants like NO₂ and VOCs into less harmful substances. **Hence, Option A is correct. **
 
• These coatings are not chemical sprays that disperse smog but instead chemically degrade pollutants through photocatalysis. **Hence, Option B is incorrect. **
 
• They are not vehicle-based filtration systems; rather, they are applied on surfaces like roads, pavements, and buildings. **Hence, Option C is incorrect. **
 
• They do not involve geoengineering or blocking sunlight; instead, they rely on sunlight to activate the catalytic process. **Hence, Option D is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Titanium dioxide is preferred due to its low cost, chemical stability, and compatibility with construction materials.
 
• The technology helps prevent formation of secondary particulate matter and ground-level ozone.
 
• Limitations include reduced efficiency under low sunlight, dust accumulation, and possible nitrate runoff causing eutrophication.

questions.question: Which Indian Ministry launched the Bharat Forecasting System (BFS) on 26 May 2025 to provide weather predictions with a 6-km resolution?

options.text: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Ministry of Earth Sciences**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Bharat Forecasting System (BFS)** was launched by the **Ministry of Earth Sciences** on **26 May 2025** to enhance weather prediction capabilities in India. • This system provides **weather forecasts** with a high resolution of **6 kilometers**, which is a significant improvement over previous models. • The BFS enhances the prediction of **monsoons, cyclones, thunderstorms, and other weather events**, helping in disaster preparedness and mitigation. • The initiative aligns with the government's efforts to utilize advanced **numerical weather prediction models** and improve weather-related services. • The BFS was developed under the leadership of the **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD)**, a part of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which is responsible for weather forecasting and climate research in India.

questions.question: The term "VANKI", recently seen in the news, is related to:

questions.question: The successful launching of the VL-SRSAM missile was conducted from the coastline of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The successful launching of the **VL-SRSAM missile** (Vertical Launch Short Range Surface to Air Missile) was conducted from the coastline of **Odisha**.
 
• The missile was developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• This missile is intended to replace the older short-range surface-to-air missile systems used by the Indian Navy.
 
• VL-SRSAM is designed to neutralize various aerial threats such as fighter aircraft, UAVs, and missiles.
 
• The missile has an operational range of **40–50 km** and incorporates advanced technologies like **dual-pulse rocket motor** and **active radar seeker**.
 
• The test was conducted at the **Integrated Test Range (ITR) in Chandipur, Odisha**, which is a premier missile testing facility in India.
 
• The successful trial is a significant step in achieving self-reliance in defense technology under the **‘Make in India’ initiative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__

 __
 
• Andhra Pradesh is known for its coastline along the **Bay of Bengal**, which stretches for around **972 km**.
 
• It is home to major ports such as **Visakhapatnam Port**, which is one of the largest ports in India.
 
• While Andhra Pradesh is a significant hub for maritime and defense activities, the VL-SRSAM missile test was not conducted here.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**__
 __
 
• Tamil Nadu has a coastline along the **Bay of Bengal** and is home to key defense establishments such as the **Heavy Vehicles Factory (HVF)** in Avadi.
 
• Though Tamil Nadu plays a crucial role in India’s defense manufacturing, the missile trial was conducted in Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**__
 
 
• Gujarat has a coastline along the **Arabian Sea**, making it strategically important for maritime trade and defense.
 
• The state is home to the **Mundra Port**, one of the largest ports in India.
 
• However, Gujarat is not known for missile testing facilities like Odisha.

questions.question: In 2025, IIT-Madras and ISRO jointly developed a semiconductor chip. What is the name of this chip?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IRIS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, **IIT-Madras** and **ISRO** collaborated to develop a breakthrough semiconductor chip named **IRIS**.
 
• The **IRIS chip** is designed to enhance India's capabilities in **semiconductor technology**, a critical area for national technological advancement.
 
• This chip aims to reduce dependency on **imported semiconductor technology** and foster self-reliance under the Indian government's **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
• IRIS is tailored to meet the needs of **aerospace applications**, ensuring compatibility with advanced satellite systems and space missions.
 
• The collaboration between IIT-Madras, a premier educational institution, and ISRO, India's space agency, marks a significant step in **academic-industry partnerships** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About IIT-Madras:**

 
 
• IIT-Madras is one of India's premier technical institutes, established in **1959**.
 
• It is globally recognized for its research and innovation in fields such as **semiconductors, artificial intelligence, and nanotechnology**.
 
• The institution has played a pivotal role in advancing India's technological landscape.
 
 
 
• **About ISRO:**
 
 
• The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) is India's national space agency, established in **1969**.
 
• ISRO is renowned for its cost-effective and innovative space missions, including **Chandrayaan** and **Mangalyaan**.
 
• It plays a key role in advancing India's space capabilities and fostering technological growth.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Semiconductor Technology:**
 
 
• Semiconductors are the backbone of modern electronics, powering devices like **smartphones, satellites, and defense systems**.
 
• India currently imports most of its semiconductors, making domestic production crucial for **economic and technological independence**.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched in **2020** by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, this initiative aims to make India self-reliant across various sectors.
 
• It emphasizes **local manufacturing, technological innovation, and reducing import dependency**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of IRIS:**
 
 
• Designed for **space missions**, including satellite communication and earth observation.
 
• Potential applications in **defense systems** and high-performance computing.
 
• Can be used for **data processing** in advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning tasks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Semiconductor Market:**

 
 
• The global semiconductor market is expected to reach **$1 trillion** by **2030**.
 
• Countries like the **USA, China, South Korea, and Taiwan** dominate the semiconductor industry.
 
 
 
• **Government of India’s Semiconductor Push:**
 
 
• In **2021**, India announced a **$10 billion incentive scheme** to boost local semiconductor manufacturing.
 
• Partnerships with global semiconductor firms have been encouraged to establish manufacturing units in India.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Semiconductor Manufacturing:**
 
 
• Requires **highly advanced infrastructure** and a skilled workforce.
 
• High initial **investment costs** and dependency on raw materials like silicon.

questions.question: Which platform was launched by the MoEFCC in January 2026 to ensure real-time institutional coordination for forest fire alerts and environmental clearances in states like Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PARIVESH 2.0**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PARIVESH 2.0** is an advanced digital platform launched by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** in **January 2026** to ensure real-time institutional coordination for **forest fire alerts** and **environmental clearances** across states like Madhya Pradesh. 
 
• This platform builds upon the original **PARIVESH** framework, introduced earlier, enhancing capabilities for **monitoring, reporting, and decision-making** in environmental management. 
 
• **PARIVESH 2.0** integrates technologies like **GIS mapping, satellite data, and artificial intelligence** to provide real-time alerts and updates, ensuring swift action to mitigate forest fires and other environmental threats. 
 
• The system allows for **inter-departmental coordination**, ensuring seamless communication between the **state governments** and the **central ministry** for faster and more efficient environmental approvals. 
 
• It provides a unified interface for stakeholders, including **government agencies, forest departments, and local authorities**, to manage environmental concerns effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PARIVESH Platform:**

 
 
• The original **PARIVESH** (Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous, and Environmental Single-window Hub) was launched by MoEFCC to streamline the **environmental clearance process** for projects.
 
• It enables project developers and environmental managers to submit applications online, track their status, and receive approvals digitally.
 
• The system reduces **paperwork**, enhances **transparency**, and speeds up the approval process for sustainable development projects.
 
 
 
• **Forest Fire Alerts:**
 
 
• India faces severe forest fire challenges, especially in states like **Madhya Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, and **Odisha**, due to their dense forest covers.
 
• Technological advancements like **satellite monitoring** and **remote sensing** are crucial for providing real-time alerts to prevent forest fire damages.
 
• PARIVESH 2.0 integrates such technologies to enhance the country's forest fire management systems.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Clearances:**
 
 
• The environmental clearance process is a critical step in ensuring that developmental projects do not adversely impact the environment.
 
• The MoEFCC is responsible for granting clearances, which involve assessments of **air quality, water resources, biodiversity, and land use**.
 
• PARIVESH 2.0 ensures faster, more transparent, and effective decision-making for approvals while safeguarding environmental sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Significance of GIS and AI in Environmental Management:**
 
 
• **Geographic Information Systems (GIS)** provide spatial data analysis, enabling better monitoring of environmental parameters.
 
• **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** helps in predictive analysis, identifying patterns, and suggesting proactive measures to mitigate risks.
 
• Both technologies are integral to platforms like **PARIVESH 2.0**, enhancing its functionality and effectiveness.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **MoEFCC Initiatives:**

 
 
• MoEFCC has launched several initiatives like **CAMPA** (Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority) and **National Action Plan on Climate Change** to combat environmental challenges.
 
• PARIVESH 2.0 complements these efforts by focusing on real-time monitoring and inter-agency coordination.
 
 
 
• **State-specific Implementation:**
 
 
• States with dense forest cover, such as **Madhya Pradesh**, **Karnataka**, and **Assam**, have been prioritized for the rollout of PARIVESH 2.0.
 
• It ensures that state governments can address unique environmental concerns effectively.

questions.question: Where is IIT Madras Global Research Foundation set to establish its first Applied Artificial Intelligence Innovation Centre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dubai CommerCity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__

questions.question: The term **'SkyCast'**, recently seen in the news, is related to:

questions.solution:

• Farmers pay a nominal premium (e.g., **2% for Kharif crops**, **1.5% for Rabi crops**) while the remaining amount is subsidized by the government.

• **Manual Verification:**

• This method is prone to delays, inaccuracies, and human biases, making it less reliable compared to advanced technologies.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the instruments onboard XPoSat?

options.text: XSPECT broadens POLIX polarimetry from 0.5–20 keV
POLIX studies black holes via X-ray polarization (8–30 keV)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**POLIX studies black holes via X-ray polarization (8–30 keV)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **XPoSat** (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) is India’s first dedicated polarimetry mission, developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (**ISRO**).
 
• It contains two primary instruments: **POLIX** (Polarimeter Instrument in X-rays) and **XSPECT** (X-ray Spectroscopy and Timing).
 
• **POLIX studies X-ray polarization** in the energy range of **8–30 keV**, focusing on objects like black holes, neutron stars, and other celestial phenomena that emit X-rays. *This statement is correct.__*
 
• **XSPECT** is designed for broad-band X-ray spectroscopy and timing, covering an energy range of 0.8–15 keV. It does not perform polarimetry. *__Hence, this is incorrect.__*
 
• The primary goal of XPoSat is to study the geometry and radiation mechanisms of various astronomical X-ray sources, with special emphasis on black holes and neutron stars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **POLIX (Polarimeter Instrument in X-rays):**

 
 
• POLIX is specifically designed to measure **X-ray polarization**, which helps understand the geometry and emission mechanisms of X-ray sources like black holes and neutron stars.
 
• It operates in the energy range of **8–30 keV**, targeting high-energy cosmic phenomena.
 
• Polarization studies provide insights into the physical processes occurring in extreme environments, such as strong magnetic fields or intense gravitational fields.
 
 
 
• **XSPECT (X-ray Spectroscopy and Timing):**
 
 
• XSPECT focuses on X-ray spectroscopy and timing analysis in the **0.8–15 keV** range.
 
• It studies the spectral properties and variability of X-ray sources but does not perform polarimetry.
 
• This instrument helps in understanding the chemical composition, temperature, and density of the emitting regions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of X-ray Polarimetry:**
 
 
• X-ray polarimetry is a unique tool to probe the **geometry of astrophysical systems**, such as accretion disks around black holes and neutron stars.
 
• By analyzing the degree and angle of polarization, scientists can infer details about magnetic field configurations and emission processes.
 
• POLIX’s capability is a significant step forward for Indian astrophysics and enhances our understanding of high-energy phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Applications of XPoSat:**
 
 
• Studying the **polarization in X-rays** emitted by cosmic sources.
 
• Investigating the **magnetic field configurations** and extreme physical conditions around compact objects.
 
• Providing complementary data for multi-wavelength observations in astronomy.
 
 
 
• **India’s Contribution to Space Science:**
 
 
• XPoSat is a significant milestone in India’s space program, showcasing the country’s advancements in **astrophysics research**.
 
• It follows ISRO’s earlier astronomical missions, such as **AstroSat**, which focused on multi-wavelength observations of cosmic sources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **POLIX vs. XSPECT:** POLIX measures X-ray **polarization**, while XSPECT focuses on **timing and spectroscopy**. Both instruments serve distinct but complementary purposes.
 
• **Black Holes and Neutron Stars:** These are some of the most extreme objects in the universe, and studying their X-ray emissions provides critical insights into their behavior and properties.
 
• **India’s Space Achievements:** XPoSat highlights India’s growing expertise in **space-based astronomical research**, building on the success of earlier missions like AstroSat.
 
• **Future Prospects:** Data from XPoSat will contribute to global efforts in understanding high-energy astrophysical phenomena and advance scientific collaboration.

questions.question: The term “Superkilonova”, recently seen in the news, is best described as:

options.text: A gamma-ray burst produced exclusively by the collision of two black holes
A radioactive explosion caused by the decay of heavy elements formed during stellar nucleosynthesis inside red giants
A rare cosmic event combining features of a neutron star merger–driven kilonova and a supernova explosion
A high-energy solar flare originating from magnetars in the Milky Way galaxy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Astronomers have reported evidence of a superkilonova—an unusually bright cosmic explosion observed about 1.3 billion lightyears away, initially resembling a kilonova but later showing supernova-like characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• A kilonova results from the merger of neutron stars, producing heavy elements like gold and platinum through radioactive decay.
 
• A superkilonova involves an additional energy source, such as fallback matter heating the ejecta, making it brighter and longer-lasting than a typical kilonova.
 
• The observed event showed traits of both a kilonova and a supernova, suggesting a new hybrid cosmic phenomenon.** Hence Option C is correct. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neutron stars:** Ultra-dense remnants formed after supernova explosions of massive stars.
 
• **Kilonovae:** Major contributors to the universe’s **heavy element (r-process) nucleosynthesis**.
